1.explanation: The bug lives in the grammar definition inside src/languages/php.js’s default export. That function builds a `className: 'function'` mode which matches both traditional functions and PHP’s arrow functions (beginKeywords: 'fn function') and sets `end: /[;{]/`, so the arrow-function body (the part after => up to the semicolon) remains inside the “function” mode. Because that mode includes hljs.UNDERSCORE_TITLE_MODE, identifiers in the expression are incorrectly marked as titles. To fix this, the arrow-function mode should be split or ended at the arrow token (=>) so that the body is parsed by the normal expression rules (including VARIABLE), not by the function rule with UNDERSCORE_TITLE_MODE.
1.bug_scenario: When using PHP’s short arrow functions (fn($x) => $x + $y;), the highlighter picks up the identifiers in the expression after the “=>” as titles (i.e. hljs.UNDERSCORE_TITLE_MODE), so both $x and $y are rendered as titles instead of variables. In the provided screenshots the actual result shows “title x” and “title y,” but the expected highlighting should treat them as variables.

bug_functions: src/languages/php.js//function parsing rule (object with className: 'function', beginKeywords: 'fn function')
2.explanation: All of the arrow‐function highlighting logic lives in src/languages/php.js inside the default export. In particular the rule with className:'function' and beginKeywords:'fn function' is used both for named function declarations and anonymous arrow functions. That rule still includes hljs.UNDERSCORE_TITLE_MODE (which forces a title after fn), so when you write an arrow function without a name it mis-applies the title style to the next token(s). Fixing this requires splitting the fn case out or removing UNDERSCORE_TITLE_MODE when beginKeywords matches only an arrow function (fn), so that no title is expected and all variables get the correct “variable” class.
2.bug_scenario: When highlighting PHP arrow functions of the form fn($x) => $x + $y (anonymous functions without a {} block), highlight.js treats the first identifier after the fn keyword and even the return‐expression variables ($x and $y) as a function name (title) instead of as parameters or regular variables. In the screenshot you can see fn is recognized as a keyword, the parameter $x is correctly recognized as variable, but the $x and $y after the arrow are marked as “title”. The expected behavior is to highlight both parameters and return‐body variables with the “variable” style.
